paragraphs.source_en: Nagayasu had said that an island of gold must have women worthy of an island of gold. Since ancient times, the island had been a place of exile for aristocrats, blessed with fine scenery and ranges of mountains. But it was, after all, a lonely and remote island; beauties from the capital must therefore be brought there to make it more pleasant still. O-Kō did not entirely believe Nagayasu's story; she was no fool.

paragraphs.source_en: From the beginning, O-Kō had never intended to be Nagayasu's virtuous wife and devoted mother of his children.
